title: Compatible calculus of fractions for quasi-isomorphisms of DG modules
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. For right DG modules $X,Y$ write $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X,Y)^r$ for degree-$r$ graded right $A$-linear maps, with differential $df=d_Yf-(-1)^rfd_X$. Write $K(A,d)$ for DG modules with morphisms $H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X,Y)$; its localization functor is $Q_A:K(A,d)\to D(A,d)$. Give $K(A,d)$ its mapping-cone triangulated structure, with shifts $M[k]^i=M^{i+k}$, differential $(-1)^kd_M$, and unchanged right graded action. The cohomology is $H^i(M)=\ker(d:M^i\to M^{i+1})/\operatorname{im}(d:M^{i-1}\to M^i)$. The quasi-isomorphisms $W_A$ in $K(A,d)$ form a saturated multiplicative system compatible with the triangulated structure as defined in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. They admit both left and right calculi of fractions and satisfy two-out-of-three. The localization is $Q_A:K(A,d)\to D(A,d)$, with the triangulated structure for which $Q_A$ is exact. The kernel consists exactly of modules for which every $H^i$ vanishes. Give the opposite categories $K(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $D(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}$ the opposite structures: the shift by $n$ is the opposite of the original shift by $-n$, and the distinguished triangles are the reversals $\operatorname{op}Z\to\operatorname{op}Y\to\operatorname{op}X\to(\operatorname{op}Z)[1]$ of distinguished triangles $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$, the last arrow induced without signs by the original third arrow. With these structures $K(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $D(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}$ are triangulated categories, the opposite class $W_A^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a saturated multiplicative system in $K(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}$ compatible with the triangulated structure as defined in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], and $Q_A^{\mathrm{op}}:K(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}\to D(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a localization at $W_A^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the sense of that definition.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-dg-homotopy-acyclic-localization] for this same associative DG algebra $A$. A degree-zero cocycle in the Hom complex is exactly a chain map, and a degree-zero boundary is $d_Yh+hd_X$ for a degree-minus-one $A$-linear map $h$. Thus its homotopy category is literally the $K(A,d)$ in our statement. The cited result gives its triangulation, the strictly full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal E$ of acyclic modules, and $W_A=W_{\mathcal E}$. No boundedness or commutativity is being assumed. For later use, $H^i$ is a functor on $K(A,d)$: a chain map preserves cycles and boundaries, and if $f-g=d_Yh+hd_X$, then on a cycle $x$ the difference $f(x)-g(x)=d_Yh(x)$ is a boundary. Identity and composition descend from chain maps.

Apply [lem-trf-triangulated-subcategory-cone-system] to the triangulated category $K(A,d)$ and its full replete triangulated subcategory $\mathcal E$ from step 1. The cone class in that result is $W_A$ by step 1. Consequently $W_A$ contains identities, is closed under composition, has both calculi of fractions (MS2 and MS3 in both directions), is invariant under integer shifts, and satisfies the triangle-completion condition MS6 of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. This application does not require a direct-summand hypothesis on $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Tag 05RG, lemma-construct-multiplicative-system, first assertion; Tag 05R2, definition-localization

proof.text: Check the remaining saturation axiom MS4 directly on cohomology. For composable $T\xrightarrow{h}X\xrightarrow{g}Y\xrightarrow{f}Z$ with $fg,gh\in W_A$, put $a=H^i(h)$, $b=H^i(g)$, $c=H^i(f)$. The map $b$ has a right inverse $a(ba)^{-1}$ and a left inverse $(cb)^{-1}c$. They agree, since for any left inverse $l$ and right inverse $r$ one has $l=l(br)=(lb)r=r$. Hence $b$ is invertible for every $i$, so $g\in W_A$. This is exactly MS4 of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. Two-out-of-three follows by the same functoriality: if two of $a,b,ba$ are invertible, the missing inverse is obtained by composing the other two inverses (for example $b^{-1}=a(ba)^{-1}$ when $a$ and $ba$ are invertible). Thus all six axioms hold.

proof.text: Take $D(A,d)$ to be the category of fractions $W_A^{-1}K(A,d)$, as in its definition, with its canonical identity-on-objects functor $Q_A$. [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives its universal property on functors and natural transformations; for this category-of-fractions model the functor factorization is an equality and is unique. This is the localization of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], with its strict functor factorizations. Apply [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6], since step 2 gives the multiplicative system and triangulation compatibility. The localization is triangulated, $Q_A$ commutes with the shifts and is exact, and its distinguished triangles are precisely the triangles isomorphic to images of distinguished triangles of $K(A,d)$. These are the stated localized cone triangles. The chosen universe bound makes the object and fraction collections sets in the ambient universe; no smallness of an index category or infinite construction in the smaller universe is used.

proof.text: If $M$ is acyclic, $0\to M$ induces isomorphisms on every cohomology group, so $Q_A(0)\to Q_A(M)$ is invertible. Exactness of $Q_A$ implies $Q_A(0)$ is a zero object, whence $Q_A(M)=0$. Conversely, each $H^i$ from step 1 inverts $W_A$ by its definition, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives $\overline H^i$ with $\overline H^i Q_A=H^i$. If $Q_A(M)$ is a zero object, it is isomorphic to $Q_A(0)$; applying $\overline H^i$ gives $H^i(M)\cong H^i(0)=0$. This proves the asserted kernel equality without assuming the converse implication of localization in advance.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-opposite-triangulated-category] first to $K(A,d)$ and then to $D(A,d)$, both now triangulated. This gives the opposite triangulations exactly as specified in the statement: shift $n$ means the original shift $-n$, and the reversed triangles have no inserted minus sign. Apply [lem-sf-triangulated-functor-opposite] to the exact functor $Q_A$ from step 4. Its opposite has the coherent shift comparisons and is exact for these structures.

proof.text: Reversal of arrows exchanges the two MS2 squares and the two MS3 cancellation conditions of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. It preserves MS1, and turns MS4 into the same implication with the order of the two composite hypotheses exchanged. Steps 2 and 3 therefore prove MS1--MS4 for $W_A^{\mathrm{op}}$. For MS5, the opposite shift by $1$ is the original shift by $-1$; step 2 gives invariance under both shifts. These checks concern the two actual calculi of fractions, rather than merely a two-out-of-three property.

proof.text: To check MS6 in the opposite, represent two opposite distinguished triangles by reversals of $T=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$ and $T^{\prime}=(X^{\prime}\xrightarrow{u^{\prime}}Y^{\prime}\xrightarrow{v^{\prime}}Z^{\prime}\xrightarrow{w^{\prime}}X^{\prime}[1])$. The given first two vertical maps unop to quasi-isomorphisms $a:Z^{\prime}\to Z$, $b:Y^{\prime}\to Y$ satisfying $vb=av^{\prime}$. Apply MS6 from step 2 to the rotated triangles $Y^{\prime}\to Z^{\prime}\to X^{\prime}[1]\xrightarrow{-u^{\prime}[1]}Y^{\prime}[1]$ and $Y\to Z\to X[1]\xrightarrow{-u[1]}Y[1]$, using $b,a$. It supplies a quasi-isomorphism $c_1:X^{\prime}[1]\to X[1]$ with $c_1w^{\prime}=wa$ and $(-u[1])c_1=b[1](-u^{\prime}[1])$. Shift by $-1$ and cancel the two minus signs; with $c=c_1[-1]$ the equations become $c[1]w^{\prime}=wa$ and $uc=bu^{\prime}$. Taking opposites gives the remaining two triangle-morphism squares, the last using $w[-1]$ and $w^{\prime}[-1]$. Also $c\in W_A$ by MS5, so the third map lies in $W_A^{\mathrm{op}}$. Replacing triangles by isomorphic ones preserves these equations and membership, since their induced cohomology maps are conjugated by isomorphisms. Thus MS6 also holds.

proof.text: Finally let $F:K(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ invert $W_A^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reverse its arrows to obtain $F^{\vee}:K(A,d)\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, defined by $F^{\vee}(X)=\operatorname{op}(F(\operatorname{op}X))$ and $F^{\vee}(f)=F(f^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Step 4 gives a unique $G:D(A,d)\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $GQ_A=F^{\vee}$. Unop its values and reverse its arrows to get $G^{\vee}:D(A,d)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal C$ with $G^{\vee}Q_A^{\mathrm{op}}=F$. These operations are inverse, so uniqueness is strict in the chosen fraction model. A natural transformation $\alpha:F_1\to F_2$ similarly gives $\alpha^{\vee}:F_2^{\vee}\to F_1^{\vee}$, whose components are the opposites of those of $\alpha$. The natural-transformation bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] lifts it uniquely $G_2\to G_1$; reversing again gives the required unique $G_1^{\vee}\to G_2^{\vee}$. Also $Q_A^{\mathrm{op}}$ inverts $W_A^{\mathrm{op}}$ since the opposite of an inverse is an inverse. This proves the localization universal property on both functors and natural transformations required by [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization].
